_comments: One category per functional area of the Orders API surface. Categories are how a human or an
agent browsing the operation catalog finds the right one — 'Orders' alone would be a bag of ten.
Fixed UUIDs rather than generated ones: these are referenced by @lookup from the operation rows,
and a stable ID means a re-push against a rebuilt database resolves to the same category instead

fields.Name: Order Lifecycle
fields.Description: Create, price, preview and confirm orders. The order is the transactional substrate and the A/R primitive, so these are the operations every other surface is built on.

fields.Name: Order Pricing
fields.Description: Resolve prices and explain how they were resolved. Read-only — nothing here writes.

fields.Name: Payments and Credits
fields.Description: Refunds, reversals and account credits. Every one of these creates a NEW payment rather than editing a captured one.

_comments: Named without an ampersand deliberately: the metadata-sync @lookup parser splits on '&'
like a query string, so 'Payments & Credits' made the reference unparseable and aborted the
whole push. Worth knowing before naming anything else that gets looked up by name.

fields.Name: Subscriptions
fields.Description: Cancellation and renewal spawning — the lifecycle events a subscription has beyond being purchased.

fields.Name: Receivables
fields.Description: Collections surfaces that cannot be expressed as a view because their predicate depends on the clock rather than on a stored value.
